title: A queue that leaves work for later
dek: A configurable job limit turns each whole-queue send into a bounded batch, leaving the rest for later drains.

sections.title: Each tick took the whole queue
sections.content:
Before this change, the worker sent every pending job in a single batch. Each call to tick drained the queue, passed the returned jobs to send, and awaited that send to the configured /jobs endpoint.

The queue helper used pending.splice(0), which removed everything from the front of the array onward. Configuration supplied the endpoint, but no batch limit. If you had 250 pending jobs, that tick handed all 250 to one send.

sections.title: Queue length decided the size of a send
sections.content:
The worker needed a ceiling on how many jobs each send received. PR #108 introduces a configurable limit with a default of 100. With 250 jobs queued, a drain at that default takes the first 100 and leaves 150. Two later drains can take 100 and then 50, assuming no new arrivals.

This is a limit on job count. As the author notes, it does not bound job memory or processing time. You can control how many jobs enter a batch without treating those jobs as equal-sized or equally expensive.

sections.title: Validate the limit, then take only that many
sections.content:
The limit enters through config.ts, which reads the BATCH_LIMIT environment variable. The module converts it to a number and validates it when configuration loads at startup:

{{CODE:0}}

An absent setting selects 100. Zero, negative numbers, fractions, and nonnumeric values fail the positive-integer check and throw the stated error. The PR does not document why 100 was chosen.

The behavioral change sits in queue.ts. The helper now accepts the count and uses it as the second argument to splice:

{{CODE:1}}

The drain removes at most that many jobs from the front of the original array. It returns those jobs for sending and keeps excess entries in the same queue. When fewer jobs remain than the limit, it takes only those available.

The worker connects the validated setting to that helper in worker.ts:

{{CODE:2}}

Each tick still awaits one send. Passing batchLimit into the drain makes the configured ceiling apply to that send; the tick does not loop through the remaining queue.

Per-tenant scheduling remains outside this change because the queue has no tenant key. The supplied diff contains no tests, and the PR documents no follow-up issues.

sections.title: One send gets a batch; the queue keeps the rest
sections.content: PR #108 replaces whole-queue drains with a configurable maximum of 100 jobs per send by default. Startup validation rejects invalid limits, the queue removes only the requested prefix, and the worker supplies the configured count. Remaining jobs wait for later drains. The guarantee is a bounded job count per batch, not bounded memory, processing time, or tenant-aware scheduling.
